title: U.S. Attorney's Office collects over $9 million in FY 2025 for Missouri district
text:
Matthew R. Price, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Missouri, and St. Louis County Circuit Judge | Official Website
Matthew R. Price, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Missouri, and St. Louis County Circuit Judge | Official Website
The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Missouri announced that it collected more than $9.7 million in criminal and civil actions during Fiscal Year 2025. According to U.S. Attorney R. Matthew Price, $9,042,015.71 was collected from criminal actions and $684,459.72 from civil actions.
In addition to these collections, the office also secured $5,514,787 through asset forfeiture actions in the same fiscal year. These forfeited assets are deposited into the Department of Justice Assets Forfeiture Fund and are used to restore funds to crime victims as well as support various law enforcement purposes.
Price stated, “The attorneys and support staff in our Monetary Penalties Unit (MPU) are committed to collecting on behalf of victims of crime and taxpayers. Through the MPU’s diligent efforts, victims of crime have received restitution for what they lost at the hands of criminal defendants. In the Western District of Missouri, defendants do not – and will not – profit from their illegal activities.”
The office also worked with other U.S. Attorney’s Offices and components of the Department of Justice to collect an additional $8,624,051.35 in cases pursued jointly by these offices; this included $52,264.86 from criminal actions and $8,571,786.49 from civil actions.
U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and department litigating divisions enforce and collect both civil and criminal debts owed to the United States government as well as debts owed to federal crime victims. Federal law requires defendants convicted of certain crimes that result in physical injury or financial loss to pay restitution directly to their victims. Criminal fines and felony assessments are paid into the Crime Victims Fund managed by the department; this fund then distributes money collected to federal and state programs supporting victim compensation and assistance.
